prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

Title, set largest at the top left of the page: bookgen
Deck beneath it: When the essays are written, the book is dressed — its back-cover blurb and its painted front cover both drawn from what the finished pages actually say.

Hero: a tailor's fitting room for a book. At the centre, a finished but naked text block stands upright on a dressing stand — plain sewn pages, no cover — and around it a jacket is being fitted: the back board, nearest the viewer, carries a neatly lettered paragraph block labeled the blurb; the front board, angled away, carries a painted scene in warm tones with the title set above it. A note at the stand: the jacket is cut from the book itself — the finished essays are read back before a word of it is written.

Feeding the fitting from the left: a reading desk where the book's own pages lie open in a fan beside the plan document, with a thin thread running from desk to back board, captioned — first the blurb is written from plan and essays. A second thread runs from desk and blurb together to a small drawing table holding a written design sheet labeled the cover design, and from that sheet a final thread to the painted front board, captioned — then the design is written, and only then is the painting made from it; the chain can stop at the design on request.

Two quiet details along the bottom:
- lower left: a jacket already hanging finished on a hook with a small do-not-disturb tag, captioned — an existing blurb or cover is left alone unless forced;
- lower right: a copy of the design sheet pinned beside plain unpainted board, captioned — a dry run shows the words and paints nothing.

One warm accent colour belongs to the painted front cover and the threads of the chain; the text block, desk, and fitting room stay in ink.
